name: Pale Congo Pink
lede: Pale Congo Pink is a pale, yellowish pink from Ridgway's 1912 plates, close kin to Hydrangea Pink, and over-represented in both Edvard Munch's paintings and our archive's paintings from India.

sections.title: A pale pink from the 1912 plates
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* places this hue at plate XXVIII, hue 7′′, tone f, scanned from an aged plate and so approximate [1]. The ISCC-NBS system later filed it in its own block [1]. It carries "Congo" in its name, but no source we checked documents why, so its origin stays undocumented here [1].

Its nearest relatives in our color graph are [[hydrangea-pink]], redder, and [[pale-flesh-color]] and [[pale-greyish-vinaceous]], close behind, all within four units [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, a color within six units of Pale Congo Pink covers at least five per cent of a canvas in 197 works, more common than 64 per cent of our named colors [3]. The painter most devoted to it is Edvard Munch, in 5 of his 50 works here, about 4.9 times his museums' baseline [3]. It is most over-represented in paintings from India, at 2.6 times expected [3]. The earliest dated appearance in our archive is 1375, over five centuries before the name's own 1912 record, a look-alike hue, not proof of pigment, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3]. These remain photographs of aged, varnished paintings, read as screen colors [3].

questions.q: Which painter in our archive is most devoted to Pale Congo Pink?
True or false: our sources document exactly why the name includes "Congo".

openers: Edvard Munch returns to this pale pink roughly five times more often than his museums' own paintings would predict.
